threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflow, main issues, and project scope before design work.

messages.text: Hello team, welcome to the project channel for the new Outpatient Check-in and Triage Process. To kick things off, let's map out the current state. Could everyone share their perspective on the existing workflow and any pain points you see regularly? This will help us with T1.

Thanks for starting. From a clinical standpoint, the biggest issue is inconsistency in triage. Depending on the nurse on duty, the same symptoms can be categorized differently, leading to variable wait times. We also lack a clear escalation path for high-risk presentations at the front desk.

Adding to that, data quality is a major concern. We often find discrepancies between the paper forms and what's entered in the EHR. This makes any kind of process audit difficult. A key success metric for me would be measurable improvement in data accuracy.
From the front desk, we have different versions of intake forms floating around. Sometimes we run out of the Spanish version. It creates confusion for both staff and patients.
Yes, the forms are a problem. Also sometimes the printer doesn't work.

Excellent point on metrics. Let's define our primary objectives. Based on the feedback, I propose we focus on: 1. Reducing average check-in to triage time by 20%. 2. Achieving 95% data accuracy between forms and EHR. 3. Standardizing the triage process to reduce variation. Does everyone agree with these as our main goals?
Those objectives are clear and cover the clinical risks. I'm on board.
Agreed. The 95% data accuracy target is ambitious but necessary. We can build our QC checks around that.
Sounds good to me.

Great. Decision D1 is confirmed. Now, to manage scope, what parts of the current process should remain untouched for this first rollout? For example, I assume the post-triage clinical pathway is out of scope.

Correct. This project should end once the patient is handed off from the triage nurse to the clinical team. We should also keep the existing appointment scheduling system as is; we're only changing what happens when the patient arrives.
Perfect. So we're agreed: the process from patient arrival to completion of triage is in scope. Appointment scheduling and post-triage care are out of scope. I'll document that.
So we don't have to change the calendar system?
That's right, no changes to the calendar system.
I've collected all the initial points on T1 and will create a draft workflow map in A1 to visualize this. I'll share it in a new thread for review tomorrow morning.
Ok, that makes sense.
Looking forward to seeing it.
Thanks, having the map in A1 will be very helpful.

threads.thread_goal: Design and validate the new workflow, forms, and triage protocol.

messages.text: Morning all. As promised, here is the first draft of the new workflow map A1. I've also created a draft of the standardized intake and consent forms A2 based on our discussion and best practices. Please review and provide feedback for T2.

Thanks. I'm attaching my draft of the Triage Protocol and Escalation Guide, A3. This is the clinical backbone of the process, defining triage categories and actions. It directly addresses the inconsistency issue. Let me know your thoughts, especially on the escalation criteria for T3.

Reviewing A2 now. The layout is clean. For data quality, can we make the 'Patient Contact Preference' and 'Emergency Contact Relationship' fields mandatory? We often have gaps there which causes issues for follow-ups.
Good catch. Yes, I can make those fields mandatory. I'll also add a small note to ensure it aligns with EHR data entry steps for T6.

On the intake form A2, the 'Reason for Visit' section should be a free-text box but with a prompt to list primary symptoms. This helps nursing staff get a clearer picture before they even see the patient.
Will the form be a PDF we can type in or does it have to be printed?
It will be a fillable PDF to support both digital entry and printing, to avoid issues like the ones @438229 mentioned earlier.
I've incorporated the feedback from @437517 and @313168. With these changes, are we ready to approve the structure and mandatory fields for the intake and consent forms?
Yes, approved from my side.
Looks good. Approved.

Now, regarding the triage protocol A3. I've based the categories on national best practice guidelines. The key is the escalation criteria on page 2. Any patient presenting with symptoms from 'List A' must be flagged in the EHR and seen by a nurse within 15 minutes. Any questions on this?
This is very clear. The 15-minute rule is a hard metric we can audit against. Is this timeframe feasible for all shifts?

It's a standard that we must meet for patient safety. The protocol includes steps for the front desk to immediately notify the charge nurse, ensuring it's achievable even during busy periods. I've already run this by the Head Nurse informally and she's supportive.
This seems very robust. If there are no other objections, I think we can approve the triage protocol and escalation criteria.
No objections. It's a solid protocol.
Looks good.

Great, D4 is confirmed. I will finalize A2 based on the feedback today. @313168, you can proceed with the formal validation for T3. My next step is to tackle T6 and ensure the EHR data entry steps are fully aligned with A2.

threads.thread_goal: Define quality control approach and how audits and incidents will be handled.

messages.text: Hi team, now that the core process is defined, let's focus on quality control. I've drafted a Quality Control Checklist A4 for daily audits (related to T4) and an Incident Log template A6 for tracking issues (for T12). Please take a look and share your feedback.
Thanks. On the checklist A4, I'd add a specific item: 'Was the triage category assigned as per protocol A3?'. This is a critical clinical safety check.
The checklist looks straightforward, which is good for daily use. Who will be responsible for completing this each day? We need to make it a clear part of someone's routine.

My proposal is that the charge nurse or shift lead for the front desk completes it at the end of their shift. It should take less than 10 minutes. They would audit a random sample of 5 check-ins from that day. For compliance, we should aim for a minimum of 4 out of 5 passing all checks.

The charge nurse is the right person for this. A 4/5 pass rate (80%) seems low for a starting point, especially on clinical items. I'd push for 90% (or 5/5 on critical items) as the minimum threshold.

Fair point. Let's set the threshold at 90% compliance overall, with 100% on critical safety checks like the one you suggested. So, we agree on the daily audit routine: shift lead completes it for 5 random cases, with a 90% pass threshold.
That works. I'll ensure this responsibility is clearly noted in the SOP.

Now for the incident log A6. The idea is for any staff member to be able to log an issue or an idea for improvement. The categories are 'Patient Safety', 'Process Issue', 'Data Error', and 'Improvement Suggestion'.
What is the conceptual difference between a process issue and a data error? Couldn't a data error be the result of a process issue?

Good question. A 'Process Issue' would be something like 'Triage room was double-booked', while a 'Data Error' would be 'Patient's date of birth was entered incorrectly'. One is about workflow, the other about information accuracy. We can add examples to the log template to make it clearer.
How often will these logs be reviewed? A patient safety incident can't wait a week.

I agree. How about this: any 'Patient Safety' log entry triggers an immediate notification to the charge nurse and clinic manager. For all other categories, this project team will review the log twice a week in a short async check-in.

That's a great suggestion. It balances immediate response with regular process improvement. So, we're decided: immediate escalation for safety issues, and a twice-weekly async review for everything else.
Where will the log be saved?
It will be a shared spreadsheet linked from the main project folder. I'll finalize A4 and A6 with the changes discussed and set up the audit routine as per T9.

threads.thread_goal: Plan training, communication, and pilot rollout details.

messages.text: Hello everyone. I have prepared the first draft of the staff training materials A5, which includes a slide deck and quick-reference sheets. I've also started an outline for the final SOP A7. This covers T5 and T10. Your feedback is welcome.

Thanks for sharing. I've reviewed the nursing section in A5. The content is accurate, but it's very theoretical. For training to be effective, we need more practical, scenario-based exercises. For example, 'A patient arrives with chest pain and difficulty breathing. What are the immediate steps according to protocol A3?'.
I agree with @313168. For the front-desk quick-reference sheet, we should use simpler language and more visuals. Let's focus on a 'Do this, then this' format. The current version is a bit dense.
Okay, those are very helpful points. I can see how scenarios would be better. What are some other key scenarios I should include for the nursing staff?
Let's add one for a non-English speaking patient, one for a patient with ambiguous symptoms, and one for handling a complaint about wait times. I can send you some bullet points.

While @435140 revises the materials, let's talk about scheduling the training (T7). We need to cover all shifts without disrupting service. I propose four 45-minute sessions: two in the morning next Tuesday, and two in the afternoon next Wednesday. Attendance at one session will be mandatory for all front-desk and nursing staff.
That schedule works for the admin team.
The schedule looks good. We'll need the revised A5 materials at least two days before the first session. So, we confirm the training schedule and that the revised A5 is mandatory for all attendees.
Excellent. Now for the pilot (T8) and patient communication (T11). I've drafted a short text for a poster and digital screens in A8. It informs patients about the new process. Please review.
The text in A8 is clear and reassuring. Approved.

For the pilot, I propose we run it the Friday after the training, from 9 AM to 1 PM. This window is usually moderately busy and will give us a good test. We'll use posters at the entrance as the main communication channel. Any objections?
The timing sounds good. We can use the QC checklist A4 and incident log A6 to gather data during the pilot.
Friday morning works. It will be a real-world test. I support this plan.
Perfect. Then we agree on the pilot start date, scope, and communication via posters.
I will have the revised A5 ready by then.
Great. I'll send out the training invites for T7 now. @435140, please prioritize the T5 revisions. @313168, you're on point for T8. I'll get the posters for T11 printed.
